title: Yet another "segmentation fault" issue with AMD GPU
body: Ollama 0.3.10 exits with `llama runner process has terminated: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)` while loading larger models on Linux with an RX 7900 XTX. `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` is about 19 GB and `gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M` is about 16 GB, both within the card's 24 GB VRAM, but they crash; models around 13 GB and smaller load fine. Ollama reports 23.5 GiB available VRAM. I think models this size used to work on an older Ollama version, but I do not know the last working version.

symptoms_visible: On Linux with an RX 7900 XTX, loading 16–19 GB models in Ollama 0.3.10 terminates the llama runner with a segmentation fault even though Ollama reports 23.5 GiB of available VRAM; models around 13 GB and smaller load.
N0.label: N0 large-model segmentation fault reported

symptoms_visible: A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` with no custom parameters attempts to load the model on the GPU and then the runner exits with a segmentation fault.
N1.label: N1 environment and trigger established

symptoms_visible: The same large model still terminates with a segmentation fault after reserving progressively more GPU overhead, including as much as 10 GB, on Ollama 0.3.10.
N2_x.label: N2_x GPU-overhead workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: On affected newer versions, a larger model can crash when requested after two smaller models have run in parallel, while two larger models handled sequentially can work; after downgrading to 0.3.6, the 21 GB command-r model loads with 100% GPU processing.
N3.label: N3 version regression demonstrated

symptoms_visible: After removing the Arch package and installing Ollama's official build with bundled ROCm, the same large-model segmentation fault remains reproducible.
N4_x.label: N4_x official bundled ROCm aftermath

symptoms_visible: Affected AMD systems load the models with Ollama 0.3.6 but segfault with 0.3.7 and later builds before the fix.
N5.label: N5 regression narrowed to 0.3.7

symptoms_visible: The reporter can load and use the previously failing large model successfully with Ollama 0.3.14-rc0.
N6.label: N6 fixed release candidate verified

symptoms_visible: The AMD large-model regression is fixed in the 0.3.14 release line, and the reporter has verified the fix with 0.3.14-rc0.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved in 0.3.14

question_patterns: Are you setting a custom context size or any other model parameters?
Does a plain `ollama run` command reproduce the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No custom context size or other parameters are set. A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` is sufficient to reproduce it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The crash occurs only with an unusually large custom context and disappears with the model's default parameters.

question_patterns: Which Linux distribution, ROCm packages, and amount of system RAM are you using?
Can you list your ROCm environment and available system memory?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Arch Linux with the distribution's ollama-rocm and ROCm 6.0.2 packages; the machine has 32 GB RAM with more than 20 GB free during the initial tests.

question_patterns: Can you share the server logs from a failing model load?
What do the logs show immediately before the runner exits?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The logs detect the RX 7900 XTX as gfx1100, report about 23.5 GiB available, select ROCm, attempt to offload the model to the GPU, wait for the server, and then report that the llama runner terminated with a segmentation fault.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied the plain trigger, server logs, package list, and memory details. These establish that the crash is not dependent on a custom context setting.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as inaccurate VRAM prediction and reserve memory by increasing OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD or manually reducing num_gpu.
solution.concrete_example: Set `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=1073741824`, increase it if needed, or lower `num_gpu` so fewer layers are loaded on the GPU.

edges.comment: The proposed memory-prediction workaround was actually tested. Reserving 1 GB and then progressively increasing the overhead to 10 GB did not stop the reporter's segmentation fault, so simple VRAM over-allocation was falsified as the main cause.

question_patterns: Does the crash depend on which models are already loaded or on parallel requests?
Can you describe any load and unload sequence that changes the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Two larger models requested together are handled sequentially and work. If two small models run in parallel and a larger model is requested afterward, the larger model segfaults when Ollama reaches it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The model crashes on its first isolated load as well as after parallel requests.
The smaller models produce different text when run in parallel.

question_patterns: Can you test an older Ollama release to identify a working version?
Does the same model still crash after downgrading to 0.3.6?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After downgrading to v0.3.6, the same command-r model works again. `ollama ps` shows it as 21 GB and 100% GPU.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same model also segfaults on 0.3.6 with an otherwise unchanged setup.
It also works on 0.3.6, but `ollama ps` reports a slightly different model size.

edges.comment: The downgrade is a handler-requested version measurement and demonstrates a product regression rather than merely an oversized model. Reports from other affected AMD users are folded into the same simulated user side where they corroborate the behavior.

solution.intent: Replace the distribution-built Ollama and system ROCm stack with Ollama's official build and bundled ROCm to address a suspected driver, ROCm, or packaging mismatch.
solution.concrete_example: Uninstall the Arch ollama-rocm package, install Ollama's official ROCm build, and retry the same model using its bundled ROCm libraries.

edges.comment: The reporter removed the Arch package and tested the official Ollama build with bundled ROCm, but the same error remained. This falsifies replacing the distribution package as the resolution for this reporter.

question_patterns: Can anyone confirm whether the regression begins in Ollama 0.3.7?
Does 0.3.6 work while 0.3.7 segfaults on the same AMD setup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. With the same affected AMD behavior, Ollama 0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 segfaults.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 work; the first failing release is much later.
0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 fails on a different affected AMD card and Linux distribution.

edges.comment: A second affected participant performed the exact 0.3.6 versus 0.3.7 comparison, folded into the simulated user side. The boundary supports the engineer's identification of the reintroduced AMD compile-flag commit in 0.3.7 as the main regression.

question_patterns: Can you test the 0.3.14 release candidate containing the fix?
Does Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 load the model that previously segfaulted?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 works great; the previously failing setup and model work successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: 0.3.14-rc0 still produces the same segmentation fault on the original command-r model.
0.3.14-rc0 loads the model successfully but takes slightly longer to start.

edges.comment: Testing the release candidate is a measurement edge. The original reporter explicitly verified that 0.3.14-rc0 resolves the failure.

solution.intent: Ship the AMD regression fix in the Ollama 0.3.14 release line after confirming that the compile-related regression introduced in 0.3.7, rather than ordinary VRAM over-allocation or Arch packaging, caused the main failure.
solution.concrete_example: Use the corrected 0.3.14 build that backs out or fixes the problematic AMD compile configuration introduced in the 0.3.7 regression window; the reporter verified the fix on 0.3.14-rc0 before the issue was treated as resolved.

edges.comment: The maintainer stated that the main issue was fixed for 0.3.14, while acknowledging that some reports in the large multi-user thread might have distinct causes. The original reporter then verified 0.3.14-rc0 successfully.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the main issue as an Ollama AMD regression introduced between 0.3.6 and 0.3.7, associated with the AMD compile-configuration change the maintainer isolated, rather than concluding that the 16–21 GB models simply exceed the RX 7900 XTX's VRAM.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: 0.3.6 loads the same 21 GB model at 100% GPU, 0.3.7 and later affected builds segfault, and the behavior also reproduces with Ollama's official build and bundled ROCm.

Must not present increasing OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD or switching from the Arch package to the official bundled-ROCm build as the resolution; overhead up to 10 GB and the official build were both tried without resolving the reporter's crash.
Must provide the corrected 0.3.14 release line as the resolution and require the original reporter's successful 0.3.14-rc0 test before declaring the issue resolved.
Must acknowledge that the thread may contain additional AMD crash causes for other configurations, while keeping this reporter's answer keyed to the confirmed 0.3.6-to-0.3.7 regression.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux and AMD GPU user: comfortable with Arch packages, environment variables, systemd logs, model concurrency tests, version downgrades, and installing an official binary, but does not claim expertise in Ollama's source or build flags.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven. Provides detailed logs and controlled comparisons, asks for documentation when configuration is unclear, follows requested tests, and reports concise confirmation when a build fixes the issue.
